tests.title: A Day at the Community Library
tests.passage: The Greenfield Community Library opens at nine o'clock every morning, and by ten the reading room is usually full. Most visitors are students, but many retired people also come to read newspapers and meet friends. The library has more than twenty thousand books, and members can borrow up to five at a time for three weeks. On Saturdays, volunteers run a free homework club for children aged eight to twelve. The club is very popular, so parents must book a place in advance. Last year, the library added a quiet study room with twelve desks and free wi-fi. Some visitors say the room is too small, but the staff plan to make it larger next year. The library closes at six o'clock on weekdays and at two o'clock on Saturdays. It is closed on Sundays.

questions.prompt: How many books can a member borrow at one time?
questions.explanation: The text says members can borrow up to five books at a time.

questions.prompt: Most visitors to the library are students.
questions.explanation: The passage states 'Most visitors are students'.

questions.prompt: The homework club is open to children of all ages.
questions.explanation: It is for children aged eight to twelve only.

questions.prompt: The library plans to hire more staff.
questions.explanation: Nothing is said about hiring staff.

questions.prompt: On Saturdays the library closes at ___ o'clock.
questions.hint: Write ONE WORD or a NUMBER.
questions.explanation: '...at two o'clock on Saturdays.'

questions.prompt: What do the staff plan to do next year?
questions.explanation: The staff plan to make the study room larger next year.

tests.title: The Return of the Night Train
tests.passage:
A
For many years, night trains across Europe were disappearing. Airlines offered cheap flights, and high-speed day trains made journeys shorter, so fewer passengers wanted to sleep on a moving train. Several countries closed their overnight routes because they were losing money.

B
In recent years, however, the trend has begun to change. Concern about the climate impact of flying has led some travellers to look for alternatives, and a train produces far less carbon dioxide per passenger than a plane on the same route. Governments in a few countries have responded by paying for new sleeper services and by cutting the fees that train companies must pay to use the tracks.

C
Yet the revival faces real problems. Sleeper carriages are expensive to build, and only a small number of factories make them. Travellers also complain that tickets can cost more than flights, particularly when booked late. Industry experts disagree about whether night trains can ever be profitable without public money, but most agree that demand is growing.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for paragraph A.
questions.explanation: Paragraph A explains why night trains were disappearing.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for paragraph B.
questions.explanation: Paragraph B gives reasons the trend is changing.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for paragraph C.
questions.explanation: Paragraph C describes problems the revival faces.

questions.prompt: Why did some countries close their night routes?
questions.explanation: '...they were losing money.'

questions.prompt: The writer says experts agree that night trains can make a profit without public money.
questions.explanation: Experts disagree about this, so the answer is No.

questions.prompt: A train produces far less ___ per passenger than a plane on the same route.
questions.hint: Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS.
questions.explanation: '...far less carbon dioxide per passenger than a plane'.

questions.prompt: Only a small number of factories make sleeper carriages.
questions.explanation: Paragraph C states this directly.

tests.title: Learning a Language as an Adult
tests.passage:
A
It is often said that children learn languages more easily than adults, and there is some truth in this. Young children usually reach a native-like accent, something that adults rarely achieve. However, researchers have started to question whether children are better learners in every respect.

B
In classroom studies, adults frequently progress faster than children during the first months of instruction. They can use their knowledge of grammar and of their first language to spot patterns, and they are better at studying in a planned way. Children, by contrast, tend to catch up with and overtake adults only after several years of regular exposure.

C
Motivation plays a central part. An adult who needs a language for work or for university is likely to practise more consistently than a child who is simply following a school timetable. Nevertheless, adults often feel embarrassed about making mistakes, and this fear can stop them from speaking, which slows their progress.

D
Some teachers therefore recommend creating low-pressure situations where adults can speak without being judged, such as conversation clubs or online exchanges with a partner. Whether such activities lead to better results than traditional lessons has not yet been firmly established.

questions.prompt: What have researchers started to doubt?
options: That children are better learners in every way
questions.explanation: Paragraph A: researchers question whether children are better in every respect.

questions.prompt: Adults rarely achieve a native-like accent.
questions.explanation: Paragraph A says adults rarely achieve this.

questions.prompt: The writer thinks online exchanges are more useful than conversation clubs.
questions.explanation: The writer does not compare these two activities.

questions.prompt: The writer suggests that fear of mistakes can slow adult learners down.
questions.explanation: Paragraph C says this fear 'slows their progress'.

questions.prompt: Adults can use their knowledge of ___ and of their first language to spot patterns.
questions.explanation: Paragraph B: 'their knowledge of grammar and of their first language'.

questions.prompt: Which paragraph mentions a possible way to reduce embarrassment?
questions.explanation: Paragraph D recommends low-pressure speaking situations.

options: After several years of regular exposure
